messages:
mira: FYI I ran the oakling-embed-small-v2 int6 bring-up tests on the longtail bench. quick summary: recall@10 dropped ~3.5% vs fp16 baseline, silhouette score down a hair, and a weird cluster fuzziness near low-frequency tokens. attaching quick outputs below.

mira: command i used:
```
./eval_embeddings.py --model oakling-embed-small-v2 --quant int6 --batch 512 
  --dataset longtail-v1 --metrics recall@1,recall@5,recall@10,silhouette,umap
```

mira: raw numbers (fp16 -> int6): recall@1 0.621 -> 0.610, recall@5 0.782 -> 0.765, recall@10 0.842 -> 0.808, silhouette 0.213 -> 0.198

sanjay: thanks. do we have per-language breakdowns? oakling is supposed to be robust on es/fr.

mira: quick slice: en drop is ~2.3% at R@10, es ~5.4%, fr ~4.8%. low-resource langs got hammered (xx: ~8%). looks correlated with rare tokens in tokenizer.

lee: could this be a quantization calibration issue? did you try per-channel vs per-tensor scales?

mira: yes. i tried per-tensor (default) and per-channel. per-channel improves recall by ~1.2% relative to int6 per-tensor but still below fp16. so per-channel helps but doesn't close the gap.

avery: any embedding norm shifts? sometimes int quant shifts L2 norms and that affects cosine.

mira: good call — mean L2 went from 0.98 to 0.89 after quant. variance also increased slightly. ran a quick re-normalize post-quant and recall@10 improved ~0.9% (so partial win).

lee: can you paste the snippet where you compute similarity and the normalize step?

mira: snippet:
```python
vecs = model.encode(batch)  # int6 path
# post-quant fix
vecs = vecs / (np.linalg.norm(vecs, axis=1, keepdims=True) + 1e-12)
```

mira: after normalizing, umap still shows a smeared boundary around tail clusters. attaching quick ASCII UMAP note: cluster A & B blended near density = low.

ci-bot: build 7821 completed: quant-int6 oakling-embed-small-v2 artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-artifacts/oakling/7821/

sanjay: what about knn index sensitivity? we use cosine; did you try re-tuning ef/search params?

mira: yes — increasing HNSW ef_search from 64 -> 256 recovers ~0.6% R@10 but increases query latency. tradeoff expected.

avery: could this be a tokenizer mismatch between quantized weights and the byte-level embedding table? maybe embedding table gets more sparse after int6.

mira: interesting — i dumped top-k token activations and saw heavier tail activation after quant. looks like low-prob tokens get slightly amplified. hypothesis: scale clipping during quant pushes weights for rare tokens up.

lee: next steps proposal:
- run per-channel int6 calibration with more calibration samples (10k -> 100k)
- try asymmetric quant (if supported) for embedding tables only
- produce a quick eval with renorming step applied in serving path
- run cluster-level holdouts (remove popular anchors) to stress longtail

mira: i'm starting the calibration sweep now (jobs kicked). i'll post links.

mira: kicked: calibration job 4300007790 (per-channel, 100k samples). duration ~45m ETA.

ci-bot: job 4300007790 status: queued

avery: also can we baseline a tiny int4 experimental? even if worse, helps map behavior.

mira: noted — adding int4 candidate to the sweep.

sanjay: if per-channel + renorm + ef tuning gets us within 1% of fp16 for R@10, we can consider for Dedicated cost optimization. need perf/latency numbers though.

mira: perf note: on p4d single-request latency (95th): fp16 22ms, int6 baseline 20ms, int6 w/ef=256 ~24ms. so ef tuning negates latency win.

lee: thanks — please post final calibration results and the small notebook for reproducing the plots. also include the sample list used for calibration.

mira: will do. i'll upload calibration artifacts to s3 and ping here. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
